frases.texto: You could call the nineteen twenty-nine crash and still go bankrupt. One man did.
Jesse Livermore traded behind a locked door with no name.
In early nineteen twenty-nine, he bet against the whole boom.
By spring, he was down six million.
Then October hit. Legend says he made a hundred million.
The public blamed him, so he hired a bodyguard.
Under five years later, he filed for bankruptcy with his mansion gone.
And that hundred million? TIME's story on his bankruptcy never mentions it.
Betting against a market can cost you more than you put in.
He called the crash. That hundred million is still a legend.
Being right about the 1929 crash should have made you rich forever. It didn't save him.
Jesse Livermore was Wall Street's most feared trader.
In early 1929, he quietly bet against the boom.
By spring, that bet had him six million dollars down.
Then the market broke, and legend says he made a hundred million.
His reward was blame, and a bodyguard.
Under five years later, he filed for bankruptcy.
TIME covered that bankruptcy. It never mentions a hundred million.
Betting against a market can cost you more than you put in.
Being right about a crash made him famous. That hundred million is still a legend.

ganchos.texto: You could call the 1929 crash and still go bankrupt. One man did.

Your best trade ever could still end like this man's did after 1929.
